root_cause.text: The driver failed to destroy page_pools and return buffers for WED RRO RX queues during device cleanup because mt76_dma_cleanup unconditionally skipped those queues when WED was active, and mt76_dma_rx_cleanup did not handle the case where WED is inactive for those queues.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the conditional skip of WED RRO queues in mt76_dma_cleanup (line "if (mtk_wed_device_active(...) && mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q)) continue;") and modifies mt76_dma_rx_cleanup to only skip returning buffers when WED is active and the queue is WED RRO, otherwise returning buffers for non-RRO or when WED is inactive. The CVE description states "All MT76 rx queues have an associated page_pool... Destroy the page_pool running mt76_dma_cleanup routine during module unload" and "returns pages to the page pool if WED is not enabled for WED RRO queues."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect buffer cleanup in mt76_dma_rx_cleanup by properly skipping WED RRO buffers when WED is active and refining the condition to avoid freeing buffers from specific WED RRO subqueues.
intent_record.what: Added an early continue for WED RRO queues when WED is active, and changed the condition for freeing the page pool buffer to exclude WED_RRO_RXDMAD_C and WED_RRO_IND queues.
intent_record.how: The function no longer processes (frees) buffers from WED RRO queues if the WED device is active; it also ensures that only queues that are not WED_RRO_RXDMAD_C or WED_RRO_IND get their buffers freed, preventing incorrect memory management when WED is involved.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incomplete cleanup by ensuring WED RRO queues are also cleaned up during teardown.
intent_record.what: Removed a conditional skip that prevented netif_napi_del and mt76_dma_rx_cleanup from being called on WED RRO queues when the WED device is active.
intent_record.how: During cleanup (mt76_dma_cleanup), all RX queues now undergo NAPI deletion and DMA RX cleanup, ensuring proper resource release for all queue types.

grouping_result.intent: Fix incomplete cleanup by ensuring WED RRO queues are also cleaned up during teardown.

relevance_review.reason: The group's changes directly address the failure to clean up WED RRO queues during teardown, which is exactly the vulnerability root cause described.

candidates.rationale: This condition, when true, causes the loop to skip WED RRO queues entirely during device cleanup, preventing buffer return and page pool destruction when WED is active.
This condition identifies WED RRO queues. Combined with the active WED check, it leads to skipping cleanup for these queues, causing the vulnerability.
This statement skips the subsequent cleanup operations (NAPI deletion and RX buffer cleanup) for WED RRO queues, directly causing the failure to return buffers and destroy page pools.
This condition prevents freeing buffers for WED RRO queues regardless of WED state, so when WED is inactive, buffers are not returned, leading to memory leak.
